items.title: Immediate high-dose-rate brachytherapy with volumetric planning for keloids: Clinical outcomes
items.authors: Nadal JA, López-Jiménez E, Rodriguez C, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate clinical outcomes and toxicity of a standardized protocol of immediate (<6 h postoperative) high-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy with volumetric planning in patients with keloids. Methods And Materials: We conducted a retrospective cohort study including consecutive patients with histologically confirmed keloids treated with surgical excision followed by immediate (<6 h) HDR brachytherapy between April 2014 and November 2025. Treatment was delivered using a uniform fractionation scheme of 12 Gy in three fractions. CT-based planning was performed in all cases, and the clinical target volume (CTV) was defined over the surgical bed. Dosimetric analysis included D90 as the primary coverage parameter. The primary endpoint was local control (LC), defined as recurrence-free interval. Secondary endpoints included late toxicity (RTOG/EORTC) and patient-reported outcomes assessed using the POSAS 3.0 scale. Results: A total of 64 keloids were included. Median follow-up was 37.5 months. The overall local control rate was 92.2%, with five recurrences (7.8%), all occurring within the first 24 months. Median D90 was 98.5%. Larger lesions (>5 cm) showed a higher recurrence rate compared to smaller lesions (12.5% vs. 7.1%). No acute toxicity was observed. Late toxicity was limited to mild hypopigmentation (9.4%), grade one telangiectasia (6.3%), and superficial atrophy (4.7%). One case of mild chondritis (1.5%) was reported. Patient-reported outcomes demonstrated minimal residual symptoms and favorable aesthetic and functional outcomes, as reflected by the patient-reported POSAS scores CONCLUSIONS: Immediate (<6 h) HDR brachytherapy with volumetric planning provides high local control and favorable toxicity in keloid treatment. A regimen of 12 Gy in three fractions is feasible and well-tolerated, representing a valid option in the multidisciplinary management of keloids.

items.title: Combined re-radiation therapy and regional or capacitive hyperthermia as a part of multimodal treatment for locoregional breast cancer recurrences in previously irradiated areas
items.authors: Kopp DH, Giovannelli AC, Mehrhof F, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Hyperthermia (HT) enhances the effects of radiotherapy (RT) and has shown benefit in recurrent breast cancer. Most existing studies focus on conventional superficial HT, whereas the efficacy of regional hyperthermia (RHT) and capacitive hyperthermia (CHT) in previously irradiated areas remains underexplored. Methods: Patients with locoregional breast cancer recurrences previously treated with RT were included in this retrospective analysis. Re-irradiation was delivered in combination with RHT or CHT and was integrated into an individualized multimodal treatment concept. HT was applied once or twice weekly immediate following RT, with temperature monitoring performed for RHT. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS) and toxicity. Results: A total of 15 patients with 17 locoregional recurrences were included. Patients received re-RT with a median dose of 50 Gy and a median of 7 HT sessions (range, 1-24 sessions; Interquartile range (IQR), 5.5-10). After a median follow-up of 30.1 months (range, 5-76 months; IQR, 13-43) two patients experienced local progression during follow-up. The estimated 2-year PFS was 75%, and OS was 60% at last follow-up. Acute and late toxicities were limited to grade 1-2 events, with no grade ≥ 3 toxicity observed. Conclusion: This retrospective analysis demonstrates the feasibility of combining RHT or CHT with multimodal treatment in patients with recurrent breast cancer and provides encouraging preliminary clinical outcomes. Despite the limitations, these findings support the integration of RHT and CHT into salvage treatment strategies and justify further prospective investigation. Clinical Trial Number: Not applicable.

items.title: Tightening the gradient: ten years of dosimetric refinement in head and neck reirradiation
items.authors: Singh S, Sen S, Kumar Singh A, et al.
items.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to quantify changes in plan quality for head and neck reirradiation (reRT) on a constant C‑arm platform. Methods: This retrospective study included 775 patients treated on a TrueBeam STx (Varian Medical Systems, Palo Alto, USA) between 2015 and 2025. Delivery transitioned from fixed-field IMRT during 2015-2019 to VMAT during 2020-2025. Planning was performed in Eclipse, with one upgrade from version 11.0.31 to 15.6.06. Endpoints included PTV D95, D98, D50, D2; different gradient indices; and doses to the spinal cord, brainstem, carotids, mandible, oral cavity, and DARS. Year-wise differences were tested using ANOVA with Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons and nonparametric sensitivity analyses. Linear models included calendar year and the log-transformed PTV volume. Results: Mean PTV D95 increased from 96.4 ± 0.5% to 99.6 ± 0.2%, while D2 decreased from 108.5 ± 1.6% to 104.0 ± 0.1%. Gradient indices decreased over the study period, indicating reduced dose spillage and steeper dose fall-off. Spinal cord and brainstem doses also declined substantially, with additional reductions in oral cavity and DARS doses. All four primary target endpoints showed significant year effects after multiplicity adjustment and nonparametric sensitivity testing. The PTV volume decreased from 700.2 ± 16.7 cc to 250.4 ± 14.7 cc, representing an approximately 64% reduction, and likely contributed to the observed improvements in gradient indices and OAR sparing. Temporal associations persisted after adjustment for the log-transformed PTV volume. Conclusion: Dosimetric outcomes improved over the study period, but these changes coincided with reduced target volume, treatment technique transition, TPS upgrade, and workflow maturation. The findings should be interpreted as multifactorial rather than as evidence of an isolated technological effect.

items.title: Increased number of chemotherapy cycles during radiochemotherapy improves overall survival without increasing toxicity in locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer patients
items.authors: Simbirova A, Löck S, Appold S, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Radiochemotherapy (RCHT) followed by immunotherapy is the standard of care for unresectable, locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (LA-NSCLC) patients. However, the impact of chemotherapy cycles and consolidation durvalumab on overall survival and toxicity remains uncertain in a real-life cohort. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 90 patients with stage IIB-IIIC LA-NSCLC treated with definitive RCHT (56-66 Gy, using weekly carboplatin/paclitaxel). Fifty of these patients received consolidation durvalumab. Chemotherapy cycles were analyzed as a stratified variable (1-4 vs. 5-7 cycles) and as a continuous predictor. Patients were also stratified by durvalumab administration. Early and late toxicities grade ≥ 2 were evaluated according to CTCAE v5.0. Overall survival (OS) was assessed via Kaplan-Meier analysis, log-rank test, Cox regression. Results: Median follow-up was 33.5 months. Patients receiving 5-7 chemotherapy cycles had significantly longer OS than those with 1-4 cycles (p = 0.048). This finding was confirmed when treating the cycle number as a continuous variable (HR = 0.75 per additional cycle; p = 0.017). Durvalumab showed a trend towards improved OS (p = 0.075). No significant increase in early or late toxicity was observed with more chemotherapy cycles. Amongst the toxicity parameters, early grade ≥ 2 anemia (27.8%) was associated with worse OS (p = 0.006). Conclusion: Receipt of 5-7 chemotherapy cycles during RCHT was associated with improved OS without an increase in grade ≥ 2 toxicity. Early anemia emerged as a key prognostic marker and was closely linked to chemotherapy de-escalation. In addition, OS estimates in durvalumab-treated patients were broadly consistent with outcomes reported in pivotal post-CRT immunotherapy trials.

items.title: FIND: a phase-II study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of erdafitinib in FGFR-altered NSCLC
items.authors: Nogova L, Malchers F, Hillmer AM, et al.
items.abstract: Introduction: FGFR alterations occur in approximately 2% of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients, predominantly in squamous cell histology (sqNSCLC). We evaluated the efficacy of the selective FGFR1-4 inhibitor erdafitinib in patients with FGFR-altered NSCLC. Methods: NSCLC patients were screened within the national Network Genomic Medicine for FGFR mutations/fusions. Patients were treated with erdafitinib in 3 cohorts: High confidence activating FGFR fusions (1), high confidence activating FGFR mutations (2), and low confidence activating FGFR alterations (3). The primary objective was the best confirmed overall response rate (ORR) in cohorts 1 and 2. Statistics analysis was based on Simon's two-stage design. Results: Between 7/2019 and 9/2022, 44.537 pts were screened in nNGM, 26 pts were enrolled in stage I of Simon's design, and 4 pts failed screening. Most pts were male (77%) and had sqNSCLC (73%). All pts were current or previous smokers. Of 22 patients on erdafitinib, 7 were treated in cohort 1, 8 in cohort 2, and 7 in cohort 3. In cohort 1, two of 7 patients achieved partial response (PR). One PR remained unconfirmed. The best response in cohort 2 was stable disease. Any grades most observed adverse events were hyperphosphatemia in 45.5%, diarrhea, and dry mouth - both in 31.8% of patients. Conclusion: According to the first stage of the two-stage Simon's design, erdafitinib showed preliminary efficacy in NSCLC with FGFR fusions. Further molecular and clinical data are needed to evaluate the efficacy of FGFR inhibition in NSCLC, especially in patients with FGFR mutations.

items.title: Efficacy and Safety of Alectinib in Pediatric and Adult Patients with ALK-Altered Advanced Solid Tumors: a phase II TACKLE Trial (NCCH1712/MK003)
items.authors: Okuma HS, Arakawa A, Hirakawa A, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) alterations occur in a range of rare malignancies; however, prospective evidence supporting alectinib beyond lung cancer remains limited. We evaluated the activity and safety of alectinib in patients with advanced ALK-altered solid tumors. Patients And Methods: In this open-label, multicenter phase II study, patients with advanced ALK-altered solid tumors received alectinib (capsule or suspension). The primary endpoint was centrally confirmed objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1, evaluated using a Bayesian design (expected ORR: 40%; threshold: 10%) in patients receiving intact capsules (Cohort A). Secondary endpoints included disease control rate (DCR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. Results: Twenty-six patients (age 8 months-78 years) with 11 tumor types were enrolled; inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor (IMT) (n=9), and neuroblastoma (n=5) were most common. ALK alterations included fusions/rearrangements (n=19), mutations (n=5), and amplifications (n=2). Median follow-up was 15.0 months. In Cohort A (n=16 with measurable disease), centrally reviewed ORR was 43.8%, meeting the primary endpoint. Among evaluable patients (n=24), ORR was 54.2% and DCR was 75.0%. Median PFS and OS were 24.9 and 38.8 months. Patients with ALK fusions/rearrangements (n=17) had ORR and DCR of 76.5% and 88.2%. All patients with IMT achieved tumor shrinkage (ORR 87.5%). Patients ≤15 years (n=11) had ORR and DCR of 63.6% and 100%, respectively. Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 15.4% (n=4), with no treatment-related deaths. Conclusions: Alectinib demonstrated meaningful, durable responses with acceptable safety across ALK-altered solid tumors, particularly in patients with ALK fusions, supporting further tumor-agnostic development.

items.title: Molecular surveillance of aggressive large B-cell lymphoma using circulating tumor DNA duplexes
items.authors: Meriranta L, Arffman M, Autio M, et al.
items.abstract: Treatment failure affects one-third of patients with aggressive large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL). However, currently available clinical tools are inadequate for determining remission and fail to detect recurrence early. We investigated the added value of longitudinal monitoring of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in plasma by targeted duplex sequencing during therapy and follow-up in high-risk LBCL patients treated in a Nordic phase II trial. Early clearance of ctDNA after the first two immunochemotherapy cycles provided a rapid pharmacodynamic measure of treatment efficacy with excellent negative predictive value (NPV, 91%) for progression. Later clearance after four cycles improved prognostication, and elevated interim ctDNA levels among those with a measurable residual disease (MRD) predicted refractory disease. At the end of therapy, MRD was a strong independent predictor of outcome, with two-year progression-free survival rates varying greatly (Hazard ratio = 18.7; 94.3% vs 18.2%, MRD negative and positive, respectively). Moreover, end-of-therapy ctDNA analysis resolved most false radiological response assessments and revealed poor targeting of post-therapy interventions to MRDpositive cases. On surveillance, ctDNA was detectable at least 3 months before systemic clinical relapse (median 6 months), while the patients with isolated central nervous system relapses had the shortest plasma ctDNA lead times. Overall, we demonstrate that ctDNA monitoring using an ultrasensitive technique provides a dynamic molecular tool to guide clinical decision-making during therapy and follow-up in patients with LBCL.

items.title: Historical Evolution of Pelvic Exenteration Surgery in Gynecologic Cancers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Brunschwig's Era versus Contemporary Practice
items.authors: Guijarro-Campillo AR, Chiva L, Domingo S, et al.
items.abstract: Background: Pelvic exenteration (PE) is a radical surgical option for locally advanced or recurrent gynecologic cancers, but its contemporary risk-benefit profile has never been systematically compared with the original Brunschwig experience. The purpose of the study was to quantify changes in major postoperative morbidity, perioperative mortality, and oncologic outcomes after PE between Brunschwig-era series (1954-1969) and contemporary series (1990-2024). Materials And Methods: This was an International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO)-registered (CRD420251009209) systematic review and meta-analysis. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched through December 2024 for studies reporting complications, mortality, or survival after pelvic exenteration for gynecologic malignancies. Two reviewers independently performed study selection and data extraction. Major morbidity was harmonized to Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher (or equivalent). Random-effects meta-analyses were performed where appropriate. All eligible studies identified were retrospective series. Results: A total of 34 studies (5478 patients; 913 historical and 4565 contemporary) were included. Major morbidity decreased from 58% (95% CI 46-68%) in historical series to 23% (95% CI 17-31%) in contemporary series, while perioperative mortality declined from 23 (95% CI 17-30%) to 3% (95% CI 2-4%). Contemporary series also reported improved oncologic outcomes, although heterogeneity and differences in follow-up precluded direct survival comparisons. Conclusions: Compared with the original Brunschwig era, contemporary pelvic exenteration is associated with substantially lower major morbidity and perioperative mortality, together with improved oncologic outcomes. These findings illustrate the remarkable technical and conceptual evolution of pelvic exenteration over the past seven decades, although direct comparisons between historical and contemporary series should be interpreted cautiously because of differences in patient selection and clinical practice over time.

items.title: Regular post-treatment surveillance is associated with improved survival in nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a retrospective study
items.authors: Wu CF, Pan QY, Yang YX, et al.
items.abstract: Purpose: Benefit of post-treatment surveillance in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), characterized by high recurrence risk, remains unexplored. We explored whether regular post-treatment surveillance facilitates earlier recurrence detection and improves survival. Methods And Materials: We identified 8,798 patients with non-metastatic stage I-IVA NPC at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center. The 1-year landmark analysis was chosen as representative of surveillance patterns, dividing patients into regular and irregular surveillance group based on surveillance intensity. Cox proportional hazards models clarified the association between overall survival (OS) and surveillance intensity, with subgroup analyses stratified by clinical stage and pretreatment Epstein-Barr virus DNA level. Survival impact of surveillance imaging for local, regional, and distant sites were also investigated. Results: Median follow-up was 64.8 months. 1-year landmark analysis comprised 4,078 and 4,720 patients receiving regular (≥ 4 visits in the first year) and irregular surveillance (< 4 visits), respectively. Regular surveillance was linked to shorter median recurrence time (26.1 versus 27.0 months) and improved OS (HR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.74-0.99; P = 0.032) after multivariable adjustment. Notably, patients receiving regular imaging surveillance for distant site had better OS (HR, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.57-0.82; P < 0.001) whereas imaging for local (HR, 1.36; 95% CI, 0.90-2.04; P = 0.140) and regional site (HR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.57-1.27; P = 0.428) did not. Regular surveillance patients with distant metastases exhibited fewer metastatic organs (P < 0.001) and earlier recurrence stages (P < 0.001), translating into prolonged post-recurrence survival (HR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.58-0.80; P < 0.001). Conclusions: Regular post-treatment surveillance, particularly distant imaging, could improve NPC survival, highlighting an urgency for evidence-based post-treatment surveillance strategies.

items.abstract: This report from the Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health lays out a foresight-driven, health-focused approach to identifying and prioritising major threats to global health over the remainder of the century. We argue that recent global shocks (including COVID-19, Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease, major geopolitical conflict, accelerating climate impacts, rapid shifts in development assistance, and the emergence of powerful artificial intelligence [AI] systems) show how quickly assumptions about stability can be overturned—and why governments and multilateral institutions must counter short-termism and localism with systematic, repeatable risk assessment and preparedness planning.

items.title: Biomarker-guided and systemic treatment strategies for meningioma
items.authors: Kurz SC, Preusser M
items.abstract: Abstract Meningiomas represent the most common intracranial tumors, overall. While a majority of tumors can be considered indolent, a subset of patients will experience repeated recurrences despite surgical and radiotherapeutic interventions. For these patients, there are only a limited number of promising systemic therapy options available. Effective drug development for meningiomas has been limited by variability in trial design, the clinical trial endpoints being used across studies, heterogeneous tumor biology and patient selection in clinical trials, and inconsistent radiological response assessment criteria. However, over the past years, tremendous progress has been made in understanding the biological and molecular underpinnings of meningiomas. Guidance on clinical trial endpoints and response assessment criteria has also improved clinical trial design and it is widely recognized that patient participation in a clinical trial remains the best way to evaluate novel therapy options and move drug development forward. In this review, we discuss factors of optimal clinical trial design for meningioma clinical trials and review and discuss the evidence supporting the use of various contemporary biomarker-guided and systemic therapy options for patients with meningioma.

items.journal: International Journal of Radiation Oncology, Biology, Physics
items.authors: Chirag Shah, Austin Sim, Erli Chen, Jason Liu, Leon Reshko, Mark P. Sittig, Mudit Chowdhary, Michael Weisman, Indra J. Das, Rishabh Chaudhari, James Bates
items.abstract: Ongoing debate exists in our specialty regarding the need for direct supervision during radiation therapy (RT) treatment. Vigorous discussion continues as to which aspects of the RT process require direct supervision to ensure high-quality RT delivery in the United States, with strong positions on both sides. Before addressing the merits of both sides, it is important to understand how our specialty reached these crossroads. RT is delivered under 3 levels of supervision: general, direct, and personal.

items.title: Trajectories of Plasma Epstein-Barr Virus DNA and Clinical Outcomes in Recurrent or Metastatic Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Treated With PD-L1 Inhibitors: A Post-Hoc Analysis of a Multicenter, Phase II Study
items.authors: Pan Z, Pei Y, Diao J, et al.
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Reliable biomarkers for predicting clinical outcomes in patients with recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (R/M NPC) treated with immunotherapy remain limited. This study evaluated the association between longitudinal EBV DNA trajectories and clinical outcomes in patients with R/M NPC receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors. Methods This post hoc analysis used data from a multicenter, single‐arm, Phase II trial evaluating the programmed cell death‐ligand 1 (PD‐L1) inhibitor KL‐A167 in patients with previously treated R/M NPC. Plasma EBV DNA was measured at baseline and at each scheduled efficacy assessment, which was conducted every six weeks until disease progression. EBV DNA trajectories were distinguished through a logistic trajectory model. Multivariable Cox models were used to calculate adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for survival outcomes. Results We identified three distinct trajectories: persistently undetectable (n = 17, 13.8%), fluctuating (n = 40, 32.5%), and persistently detectable (n = 66, 53.7%). Compared with the persistently undetectable group, HRs of death were 4.96 (95% CI, 1.60–15.40) and 12.59 (95% CI, 4.01–39.51) for the fluctuating and persistently detectable groups, respectively. HRs of disease progression were 1.96 (95% CI, 0.97–3.96) and 3.22 (95% CI, 1.56–6.67), respectively. Conclusion This study suggests that plasma EBV DNA trajectories could be a promising biomarker for monitoring treatment response and longitudinal risk stratification.

items.title: [Review] Emerging novel therapies for the treatment of hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia
items.authors: Hanny Al-Samkari
items.abstract: Hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia is the second most common heritable bleeding disorder worldwide, with a prevalence more than twice that of haemophilia, and is the most morbid inherited bleeding disorder of women. As an autosomal dominant vasculopathy due to dysregulated angiogenic signalling, patients with hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia develop telangiectasias and arteriovenous malformations which cause numerous complications. These complications include moderate-to-severe chronic epistaxis, gastrointestinal bleeding, iron deficiency anemia, and requirement for intravenous iron or red cell transfusion.

items.title: Evaluation of PET-detected nodal upstaging and planning target volume expansion in esophageal cancer radiotherapy planning
items.authors: Jain S, Maheshwari B, Bellige AR, et al.
items.abstract: Background: While 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET/CT) is known to influence staging, its quantitative impact on clinically meaningful target volume expansion remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated whether PET-detected nodal upstaging is associated with significant planning target volume (PTV) expansion. Methods: Fifty consecutive eligible patients with esophageal cancer undergoing computed tomography (CT)- and PET-based radiotherapy planning between January 2018 and January 2022 were retrospectively analyzed, with no predefined target sample size. Clinically significant PTV expansion was predefined as a > 10% increase from CT-based to PET-based planning. Associations between PET-detected nodal upstaging and PTV expansion were evaluated using Fisher's exact test, logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and nonparametric testing. Given the limited number of events, a parsimonious multivariable model and threshold sensitivity analyses were additionally performed. Results: Patients with nodal upstaging had a significantly higher risk of > 10% PTV expansion (48.0% vs. 16.7%; absolute risk difference 31.3%, 95% CI 6.7-55.9%; p = 0.032). The median percent PTV change was significantly higher in patients with nodal upstaging (9.49% vs. 0.31%; Wilcoxon p < 0.001). In a parsimonious multivariable model adjusting for tumor length, nodal upstaging remained independently associated with clinically significant PTV expansion (odds ratio (OR) 4.38, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.12-17.10; p = 0.033). Model discrimination was acceptable (area under the curve (AUC) 0.7254), with stable performance on bootstrap internal validation (bootstrap mean AUC 0.733). Sensitivity analyses using alternative expansion thresholds (> 5%, > 10%, and > 15%) demonstrated directionally consistent associations. Patients meeting the PTV expansion threshold also demonstrated significantly greater increases in lung dose-volume burden (mean lung dose, and lung volumes receiving 5 Gy and 20 Gy; all p < 0.001) in paired dosimetric comparison, supporting the clinical relevance of this threshold. Conclusion: During esophageal cancer radiotherapy planning, PET-detected nodal upstaging was independently associated with clinically meaningful target volume expansion. The association was consistent across alternative expansion thresholds and in bootstrap internal validation, and a paired lung dose-volume comparison indicated that the expansion threshold corresponds to a measurable increase in lung dose burden.
